t06-parent-promoted.blockerMarkdown: Held by the owner (2026-10-17) until the AccessKit epic merges into main: the off-screen rows' records must be hidden on main's AccessKit model (s06b). Work kept on local branch wip/s04-parent-viewport (a6d5808).

s00-measured-leaves.summaryMarkdown:
Passed. The final s00 mechanism records each measured leaf requested under view retention with its owning view and whether its style fixes its size in every parent. On the next frame it builds (`mark_view_dirty`, counted once) every view holding a non-text leaf that is not fixed or that Taffy measured to size it. Splice takes those views as gaps from `dirty_views`, so their ancestors are spliced, not built, and the layer and list-row checks honour the dirtiness. Text keeps its carry and replay paths, and fixed measured leaves keep their view reusable (`views_reused > 0`, 0 builds). With view retention off nothing is counted or changed. No frame-local closure crosses frames.

**Accepted cost:** every view holding a non-fixed measured leaf is built on each drawn frame. This covers `uniform_list`/`list`/`VirtualList` with `Infer` and RayX's markup `inline_flow`, and matches d-retained-measured-leaves, which defers measurement replay to a later optimization driven by `views_built_for_measured_leaves`. Defaults (`ListSizingBehavior::Auto`, img, svg, text) are unaffected. The ML-1 group (9 tests) and the ML-2 oracle cover the cases. The sprint checks are fresh at revision 13.

s01-horizontal.summaryMarkdown:
Passed, with no findings.

**Axis-generic code.** `begin_virtual_list` takes the list's axis and works along it: content size and start, overscan reach from the viewport's extent, and placement by the list's own origins. The axis-generic parts are `row_slot` (whole viewport across the axis), `hidden_in_view`, the Extend test (cross-axis offset unchanged), `rows_region`, `rows_overflow`, and the spill test and extent in `end_paint_rows`. The remaining y-only code in lists.rs belongs to the vertical-only `list` element (`list_row_top`, `held_rows_land_alike`, `end_list`) or already handles both axes (`step`/`delta`, `drawn_alike`, painted region). The content-ordering helpers `apart_in_order`/`gather` in scene.rs already take runs along either axis. `uniform_list` and `list` pass `Axis::Vertical`. Sticky lists stay ineligible because `carried` is `sticky_items.is_empty()`.

**Tests.** `horizontal` asserts composite-or-repaint each frame (repainted ≤ 1, the same tolerance as the vertical `rows` group), ineligible 0, kept > 0, closure rows equal to `list_rows_rendered` and a mean ≤ 2. It also compares a horizontal history with layers off, and covers width changes of 7.5 and 11 px plus a cross-axis wheel. `horizontal_oracle` covers fractional widths, gap and padding at scales 1 and 1.25, plus seeded `describe_rendered_frame` histories. The removed ineligible horizontal case is superseded as HZ-1 requires. The sprint checks are fresh at revision 28.

s02-sticky.summaryMarkdown: Passed. A sticky `VirtualList`'s layer holds ordinary rows only: every candidate in the layer's reach is excluded by the `outside` predicate, and a layer found holding one is repainted. The active stack and the incoming candidates in `rendered_range` are rendered and prepainted after `end_rows` (hit first) and painted after `end_paint_rows` (above the composited layer), in the list's scroll context and clip, as the rows themselves. They keep the sticky wrapper, `when_stuck` and `on_sticky_state_changed`, in `compare_sticky_render_layers` order. `sticky` (now with dense candidates in both directions and the held-row invariant) and `sticky_oracle` cover ST-1 and ST-2. The RayX consumer test is updated in a paired change. The sprint checks are fresh at revision 37.

s03-synchronized.summaryMarkdown: Passed. A `SynchronizedOffset` list gets its own list layer keyed by its id, at the shared handle's snapped offset, with the driver's published offsets and dependent notifications counted as its scroll (`invalidate::painted_synchronized`). This holds only while what holds the list clips it within its bounds. Otherwise it is counted ineligible and drawn exactly as before. Paint is unchanged in every mode, so frames with fast mode off are today's. `synchronized` covers both axes (counters, comparisons with layers off, whole-frame histories) and the unclipped ineligible case. Consequence recorded for s05: RayX's ListView, TreeView and DataTable body in this mode get a layer only where their container clips them. The sprint checks are fresh at revision 44.

s05-rayx-kinds.summaryMarkdown: Passed. RayX's `virtual_list_layer_kinds` groups prove the consumer on real components: a sticky ListView with two levels, a horizontal ListView, a TreeView with sticky roots, a click reaching a stuck header first on a composited frame, and a DataTable whose `SynchronizedOffset` rows composite from their layers with exactly one frame per wheel turn. The DataTable fixes match the owner's choice (a) recorded in d-consumer-proof: a `ParentViewport` leaf header row, `SynchronizedOffset` filler rows, column bounds in shared cells with the table and fixed-column bounds written only on change, and rows clipped in `overflow_hidden` containers. Also `ScrollableMask` publishing through gpux's new `ScrollHandle::publish_wheel_offset`, with the container's own clamping and edge behaviour (gpux test `a_forwarded_wheel_turn_composites_in_one_frame`). The sprint checks are fresh at revision 56 on the s05-only tree.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Resolved. The style flag is replaced by recording, in the Taffy measure callback, every non-text leaf whose measurement can set its size. That is an axis of `known_dimensions.or(style size resolved against parent_size, with the aspect ratio applied)` left `None`; ContentSize mode uses `known_dimensions` alone, mirroring taffy 0.14 `compute_leaf_layout`. This catches percentages of an indefinite parent and the flex automatic-minimum probe, and keeps leaves of definite size reusable. New cases `PercentOfAutoParent` and `DefiniteFlexChild`. The transition case the new mechanism cannot see is filed as lk-s00-F4.

Resolved. The counter now counts once per view, at draw start, when `Window::draw` marks a measuring view dirty that was not already dirty. It no longer counts refusals inside `keep_retained_nodes`, so the double count through `reuse_kept_layout` and the layer-content count are gone. The tests bound the count exactly per mode (0 without view retention, 0 in the definite case with `views_reused > 0`), with stats reset after `set_fast_mode`.

Resolved. The measuring view is `mark_view_dirty`'d, which dirties its ancestors exactly as a notify does. With splice on, `splice_layout` takes dirty nested views from `dirty_views` as gaps (splice.rs:399), and the view is not in `notified`, so its ancestors are spliced, not built. Without splice, they cost what a notify of that view costs. The dirtying happens before `invalidator.set_dirty(false)`, so it schedules no extra frames.

Resolved. `Window::note_measured_owner` records every measured leaf requested under view retention with `fast::layout::measured_size_is_fixed(style)`. That means an absolute width and height, plus an absolute `min_size` on both axes or overflow Hidden/Scroll on both axes. Before clear, the owners of every non-text leaf that is not fixed, or that Taffy measured to size it, are built on the next frame, so a leaf that can become indefinite is never kept. Checked against taffy 0.14: a fixed leaf's size never comes from its measurement. Its InherentSize probes resolve the style size (leaf.rs:61, 147). The flex base size takes the definite main size. The automatic minimum is skipped by an absolute min size or a non-visible overflow (flexbox.rs:1037). The intrinsic-main path (flexbox.rs:1405) and the hypothetical cross size (flexbox.rs:1819) use the preferred size, and the baseline and absolute-child ContentSize calls pass both dimensions. The stated residual (a fixed leaf probed while kept) therefore has no reachable size effect. Regression: `a_kept_leaf_keeps_its_size_when_its_parent_becomes_flex` (red on the previous source) and `a_kept_leaf_keeps_its_size_when_its_parent_loses_its_height`.

Resolved. `measure_item` records with `finish_recording_dependencies_as_own`, which does not push its ranges into the parent's `nested`, so the measured row's reads stay among the owning view's own dependencies, which splice decides on. A kept no-layer frame replays them with `replay_dependencies_as_own` before carrying states and lines, so the view's record keeps them for `retained::reusable`. Regression: `an_update_only_the_measured_row_read_measures_it_again` (an entity only the measured row reads, updated without a notification, and with the Beside view notified), under view retention and splice.

Resolved. `note_notify` counts every `App::notify` (at entry, before deduplication) of a watched view whenever a watch exists. `note_scroll_notify` counts the scroll-sent notifications: div's handle-less wheel branch and both `ScrollHandle::publish_offset_inner` blocks. The no-layer keep refuses when notifications since the measurement exceed scroll notifications, or when the owner is another view, and carry refreshes the baselines. Scroll notifications that are not marked (RayX's scrollbar `cx.notify(view_id)`) count as changes, which is conservative. Regression: `a_notification_of_the_lists_view_measures_it_again` (`Rc<Cell>` state plus a bare notify) under view retention and splice. The scroll-only tests still keep the size.

Resolved. Edges round ties down while snapping (`round_half_down` = `ceil(x - 0.5) + 0.0`, with negative zero normalized). The rule is invariant under whole-pixel moves, equals `round_half_toward_zero` on non-negative values, and matches `fast::glyphs`. Default-mode output therefore changes only for negative ties. The `snap_offset` doc and docs/fast-mode.md are corrected, and the underline test expects the new rounding. Regression: `fast::tests::half_pixel_edges`.

Resolved. `begin_virtual_list` and `begin_rows` take an `outside` predicate. `VirtualList` passes a binary search over its sorted candidates, so every candidate in `needed` is kept out of the plan, and Extend is refused while any held row is a candidate. The planned rows are never candidates, so the prepaint loop's peek diverts no overscan row. Only the active stack and the candidates in `rendered_range` (rendered separately when layered) are drawn above the layer. `uniform_list` passes `|_| false`. Regression: `sticky::no_candidate_in_the_layers_reach_is_held` covers `Dense` (every 4th row) on the top and left edges plus `Levels`, over down, repaint, up, repaint and down runs. It checks the held rows and primitives against the reference every frame, with at least 30 composited frames, and failed on the old in-view-only set.

Resolved. A paired RayX change, uncommitted, to land with the gpux commit, replaces the ineligibility test with `a_list_view_with_a_sticky_policy_composites_its_ordinary_rows` in `rayx_components_core/tests/virtual_list_layers.rs`. Over 60 frames it asserts no ineligible bypass, one composite or repaint per frame, 1–2 sticky rows drawn, and repainted ≤ 1. d-sticky-over-layer is amended (planRevision 7) to describe the sticky rows drawn as frame content after `end_rows` and `end_paint_rows`, and why the `extra` wording changed.

Resolved. Both clips are removed, so a `SynchronizedOffset` list paints as before in every mode, fast mode off included. Eligibility is now gated instead. The list is `carried` only when the content mask of what holds it lies within its bounds (`mask.intersect(&bounds) == mask`, read in prepaint before the list pushes its own rectangular mask). On such frames the layer's viewport clip and the prepaint hitbox clip coincide with what the frame without a layer shows. Otherwise the list is counted ineligible and drawn as today. Regression: `an_unclipped_synchronized_list_is_ineligible_and_draws_as_without_layers` (`clipped: false`, compared with layers off, ineligible ≥ 30, no rows kept, no list layer) fails with the gate forced open. The clipped page variant (an `overflow_hidden` container of the list's size, the DataTable-body pattern) keeps the four existing tests passing.

Resolved. The second frame came from `ScrollableMask`'s old `request_offset(Programmatic)` path, a queued offset taken in at the next prepaint with a deferred notify, which `publish_wheel_offset` replaces. The DataTable test keeps draw-on-flush on, draws every frame the table asks for (`run_until_parked`, plus a draw only if none happened), and asserts exactly one frame per wheel turn on each of the 40 measured turns. A deferred frame left behind by a turn would be drawn at the next turn's `run_until_parked` and fail that turn's count, so the one-frame assertion covers it. Composite-with-rows-kept on at least 38 of 40 turns and cells shown are asserted as before.

handoffMarkdown: RayX groups: rayx_components_core/tests/virtual_list_layer_kinds.rs (sticky ListView at two levels, horizontal ListView, TreeView with sticky roots, click on a stuck header) and rayx_components_datatable/tests/virtual_list_layer_kinds.rs (DataTable synchronized rows). DataTable fixes (owner choice (a)): header leaf row as a ParentViewport h_virtual_list with its own handle state; filler cells through a SynchronizedOffset list; header cell bounds in shared cells, table/fixed-column bounds written only when they move; rows' lists clipped to their width; ScrollableMask publishes its turn via gpux's new ScrollHandle::publish_wheel_offset (test in virtual_list_layers::synchronized).
